title: Garou and the Tatar Yoke
summary: A tribal quarrel behind Mongol rule in Russia.

claims.text: With Kin of their own among the Mongol clans, the Shadow Lords quietly backed the Tatar Yoke over Russia from about 1240 to 1480.
When the Silver Fangs demanded those families leave Fang lands, the Shadow Lords answered that they had no hold over the Mongols.
Ivan III's marriage to Sophia Paleologos, niece of the last Byzantine emperor, gave the Silver Fangs the new royal blood they wanted for their Kin.

title: The White Nights
summary: Russia's summer solstice and its effect on the Kindred.

claims.text: During the White Nights of June, the sun stays up for two or three weeks north of St. Petersburg.
Kindred there are at their weakest and must sleep through it, while Garou roam freely and the Inquisition and Orthodox Church hunt the sleeping vampires.
The oldest and most powerful vampires of Russia travel south for the season or hide where no one can find them.
Russia's Umbral forests are rich with Wyldlings and spirits, so beautiful they move even hard-hearted Garou, and wind spirits gossip under the great trees.
Where the land was ravaged, pollution Banes walk instead, tree spirits sour into Blight Children and the Leshii forest spirits twist into violent horrors.
In the worst places the Gauntlet has worn thin, spirits drift in and out unknowing, and mortals who stray there are rarely seen again.
Russian cities in the Umbra are grey geometric mazes linked by twisting pipes, where spirits become cold automatons and people walk like the dead.

title: The Great Zmei
summary: The seven dragons of Russian legend.

claims.text: Baba Yaga summoned seven great dragons, the Zmei, named in Russian lore as Shazear, Goluko, Trevero, Illyana, Gregornous, Sharkala and Rustarin.
They began as Wyld creatures of an older age before the Wyrm's corruption dragged them down, and each resembles the Wyrm.
For years they ruled wide dragon lands that people feared to enter, until the Silver Fangs of Russia drove them into slumber.
Russian lore remembers mages, not Garou, as the dragon-slayers of old.
